skill.name: youtube-downloader
skill.description: Download permitted YouTube videos or MP3 audio with selectable quality, format, and output directory settings through a yt-dlp wrapper.
skill.summary: Downloads permitted YouTube media with quality, format, audio-only, and destination controls.
skill.author: ComposioHQ

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown findings are false positives because they are fenced examples or inline option names, not Ruby backtick execution. The real risks are Python subprocess calls that install yt-dlp, process a user-provided URL, and run a downloader with user-controlled destination settings. No prompt injection was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Runtime package installation modifies the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Declare yt-dlp as a pinned dependency installed before runtime. Remove --break-system-packages and require user confirmation for any install step.

remediation.issue: User-controlled URLs are processed by an external downloader.
remediation.suggestion: Validate URL scheme and domain before invoking yt-dlp. Keep list-form subprocess calls and reject unsupported or local resource inputs.

remediation.issue: Custom output paths are not restricted.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the output path and restrict writes to an approved output root. Reject parent traversal, system paths, and credential directories.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 only probes yt-dlp with a fixed --version argument. No user input is included, so this is a safe dependency check rather than command injection.

Line 19 auto-installs yt-dlp with pip and --break-system-packages if the binary is missing. This pulls code from the package index and modifies the runtime environment without an explicit consent gate.

Line 24 runs yt-dlp against a user-supplied URL to fetch metadata. Arguments are passed as a list, which reduces shell injection risk, but the external downloader still processes attacker-controlled network input.

Line 92 executes the assembled yt-dlp command using user-controlled URL and output directory values. The list form avoids shell expansion, but the external process can still download remote content and write to the chosen destination.

content.user_title: Download YouTube Videos and MP3 Audio
content.value_statement: Saving permitted YouTube media for review or offline work can be slow and error-prone. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through quality, format, and audio-only downloads using yt-dlp.
actual_capabilities: Downloads a single YouTube video using yt-dlp.
Exports video as MP4, WebM, or MKV.
Lets users choose an output directory.
Shows title, duration, and uploader before download.
limitations: Requires network access and a working yt-dlp installation or package install.
Downloads only single videos because playlists are disabled.
Does not verify copyright, license, or creator permission.
May fail if YouTube changes access rules or blocks the environment.

use_cases.title: Archive Approved Training Clips
use_cases.description: Save a permitted training video in a consistent format for internal review sessions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Offline Research Media
use_cases.description: Download a single source video for lawful offline analysis when connectivity is limited.

use_cases.title: Extract Reference Audio
use_cases.description: Create an MP3 from an approved video for transcription, accessibility review, or note-taking.

prompt_templates.title: Download Default Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Download this permitted YouTube video at the default quality to the default output folder: [URL]. Confirm the title and saved location.

prompt_templates.title: Extract MP3 Audio
prompt_templates.scenario: Audio-only request for review or transcription.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract MP3 audio from this permitted YouTube video: [URL]. Use the default output folder and report the duration.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Quality and Format
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with explicit media settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Download this permitted video as 720p WebM to [folder]: [URL]. Report the title, uploader, and final saved location.

prompt_templates.title: Process Review Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using repeated single-video downloads.
prompt_templates.prompt: For these permitted single-video URLs, download each at the smallest acceptable review quality into [folder]. Summarize successes, failures, and storage impact.

output_examples.input: Download a permitted video in 720p MP4.
output_examples.output: The video is downloaded with the requested quality and format. The response includes title, duration, uploader, and saved file location.

output_examples.input: Extract MP3 audio from a permitted video.
output: The result is saved as an MP3 in the chosen output directory.
Any download error is reported with the failing step.

output_examples.input: Download a permitted WebM copy to a project folder.
output_examples.output: The skill uses the chosen folder and format, then reports whether the download completed or failed.

best_practices: Download only media you own, have permission to use, or may lawfully access.
Use the default output folder unless a project requires another approved location.
Choose lower quality for drafts and higher quality only when needed.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass platform rules, paywalls, or copyright restrictions.
Do not download playlists or large batches without storage and permission checks.
Do not direct output to system, credential, or application directories.

faq.question: What does this skill download?
faq.answer: It downloads a single YouTube video or extracts MP3 audio from a single YouTube video.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it download playlists?
faq.answer: No. The script passes a no-playlist option and is designed for one video at a time.

faq.question: Can I choose video quality?
faq.answer: Yes. Supported choices are best, worst, 1080p, 720p, 480p, and 360p.

faq.question: Does this skill install anything?
faq.answer: The script can install yt-dlp with pip if it is missing. Review this behavior before use.

faq.question: Does it check usage rights?
faq.answer: No. Users must confirm they have permission or a lawful basis before downloading media.
